Bank of America Family Office Study: Next Generation Set to Reshape Family Offices


##


A quarter have seen a transition within the last decade, and among those offices, only 37% said their incoming principal was very prepared.


## Key points


- Private markets, direct investments and other alternative assets, including sports ownership, are shaping the future of family office portfolios.
- Family offices look to strengthen governance and education ahead of succession.
- Credit and A I


AI


are expected to be used strategically by the next generation.

NEW YORK, New York


N.Y.


– The[Bank of America Family Office Study: Building for Generations](https://www.privatebank.bankofamerica.com/articles/family-office-report.html) reveals that family offices are entering a pivotal period of transformation as many family offices prepare for leadership transition, and the next generation of principals brings different perspectives on how wealth is invested, managed and preserved.


The study found that generational influence is already shaping family office priorities as they build across generations. Among family offices with a potential next-generation principal, seventy nine percent


79%


predict alternative investments will represent a larger portion of portfolios going forward, while seventy seven percent


77%


expect philanthropic priorities to evolve with the next generation.


*“Today’s family offices are building for the future while balancing continuity and changes today,”* said **Elizabeth Thiessen, Head of Family Office at Bank of America Private Bank** . *“The families best positioned in this transition recognize that preparation goes well beyond identifying the next leader. It requires strong governance, a shared vision and the ability to adapt to changing opportunities and priorities across generations.”*


## Alternative assets shape diversification in future family office portfolios


- **Private equity remains a cornerstone of alternative allocations** , representing twenty seven percent


27%


of family office alternative portfolios, while fifty nine percent


59%


of offices plan to increase exposure over the next three years.
- **Direct investments continue to attract family offices seeking long-term value creation,** with thirty eight percent


38%


citing ownership stakes as a top wealth-generation opportunity. Private equity is number one


No. 1


( fifty one percent


51%


).
- **For most family offices, capital growth is the investment priority,** outranking income generation and balanced positions.
- **Sports ownership is gaining traction.** Four in 10 family offices hold sports investments today. Offices with at least one Gen Z or Millennial principal are most likely to own sports teams or sports-related assets.
- **Art can represent a significant store of wealth.** Three in 10 family offices with art holdings say that the family’s collection is valued at more than twenty five million dollars


$25 million


.


## Family offices focus on closing readiness gaps as leadership transition nears


- **Most family offices have identified a successor ( eighty three percent 83% )** , **** but only twenty seven percent


27%


of offices have a trust distribution policy or guiding principles in place.
- **Governance and family education remain central to successful transitions.** Nearly all ( ninety one percent


91%


) agree they help keep families aligned on priorities, yet fewer than half ( forty percent


40%


) of offices have a formal family education program.
- **Nearly nine in 10 agree governance structures help reduce family disagreements** , and seventy three percent


73%


plan to adopt additional governance structures in the next three years.
- **Family dynamics remain the top governance challenge ( forty five percent 45% )** , followed by the complexity of shared assets ( thirty seven percent


37%


) and undefined family expectations ( thirty six percent


36%


).


## Credit emerges as a strategic wealth tool for the next generation


- **While credit use is nearly universal among family offices ( ninety two percent 92% ),** only twenty seven percent


27%


use leverage consistently as part of a long-term wealth strategy.
- **Today, family offices primarily use credit to support real estate investments ( forty five percent 45% ),** remain invested through market cycles ( forty two percent


42%


) and bridge short-term liquidity needs ( thirty eight percent


38%


).
- **Future principals may take a more strategic approach to borrowing.** Nearly eight in 10 family offices ( seventy seven percent


77%


) believe the next generation will be more interested in using credit to build wealth.
- **Business-owning families are more likely to embrace credit as a wealth-building tool,** with more than twice as many using leverage as part of a long-term wealth strategy compared to families without a wealth-generating business ( thirty two percent


32%


versus


vs.


fourteen percent


14%


).


## A I


AI


becomes a competitive advantage for modern family offices


- **A I AI adoption is common across family offices** , with forty two percent


42%


of family offices reporting regular employee use, primarily for data analysis ( sixty four percent


64%


), meeting summaries ( fifty seven percent


57%


) and automation ( forty nine percent


49%


).
- **Demand for technology continues to grow** , and eighty three percent


83%


of family members expect their family office to implement new technology solutions.
- **Family offices view A I AI as a strategic advantage, not just an operational tool.** Eight in 10 believe A I


AI


has the potential to improve investment returns, rising to eighty eight percent


88%


among family offices with next-generation involvement.

## 2026 Bank of America Private Bank Family Office Study methodology


In the 2026 Bank of America Family Office Study, Escalent, a research firm, surveyed 355 family office decision makers in the U S


U.S.


The firm also spoke with executive-level roles, including principals, C-suite, president/founders and investment professionals. The offices range from twenty five million dollars


$25M


in assets under management to more than five billion dollars


$5B


, with the majority over five hundred million dollars


$500M


. The average office tenure is 11–20 years. The survey was fielded in January and February of 2026.


## Frequently asked questions


### Question: What family office services does Bank of America Private Bank provide?


**Answer:** Bank of America Private Bank’s Family Office practice supports families across governance, investment strategy, strategic credit, trust and estate planning, philanthropy, family education, treasury management, bill pay, accounting and reporting, and specialty asset management. Dedicated Family Office Strategists work alongside Private Bank teams to help families navigate complex decisions related to operating businesses, multigenerational wealth and family governance.


### Question: What differentiates Bank of America’s approach to family office services?


**Answer:** Bank of America Private Bank is differentiated by its ability to connect family offices with capabilities across the broader bank. Through coordinated engagement with Global Commercial Banking, Global Corporate & Investment Banking and Global Markets, families can access treasury and liquidity solutions, commercial and corporate lending, capital markets capabilities, and other specialized resources. Private Bank advisors remain at the center of the relationship, helping ensure a coordinated experience across the enterprise.


### Question: How does Bank of America Family Office Solutions use technology?


**Answer:** Technology plays an important role in helping family offices manage growing operational complexity. Through a fully outsourced infrastructure solution, families can access aggregated reporting, accounting, bill pay and treasury management capabilities. These services are augmented by CashPro®, Bank of America’s integrated digital banking platform that helps businesses and family offices manage cash, payments, and liquidity, while delivering insights on how to make their business operations more efficient.
